query: Eutectic high-entropy alloys contain dual-phase lamellar colonies with numerous internal boundaries, where microcracking can initiate and lead to catastrophic damage during room-temperature tensile deformation. Conventional processing commonly raises strength at the expense of ductility, while the wide range of previously proposed microstructural-design and processing strategies has not eliminated room-temperature brittleness and limited tensile ductility. Under these constraints, what single intervention could improve both strength and room-temperature tensile ductility? State one testable hypothesis that identifies the intervention, explains its mechanism, predicts outcomes relative to the unmodified lamellar-colony baseline, defines its boundary conditions, cites supporting prior evidence, and proposes an experiment whose result would falsify the hypothesis.

generation.hypothesis: A controlled sub-annealing heat treatment that promotes nanoscale segregation at colony boundaries will induce the formation of thin, ductile interfacial films, thereby blunting microcrack initiation and propagation and improving both strength and room‐temperature ductility in eutectic high-entropy alloys.
generation.material_initial_state: Eutectic high-entropy alloys consisting of dual-phase lamellar colonies with numerous internal boundaries that serve as microcrack initiation sites during room-temperature tensile deformation.
generation.intervention: Apply a controlled, sub-annealing heat treatment designed to trigger minor solute segregation and induce the formation of nanoscale, ductile interfacial films along the lamellar colony boundaries.
generation.conditions: Identical alloy compositions are used; the annealing temperature and time are carefully selected to be high enough to drive interfacial segregation but low enough to avoid excessive phase coarsening or formation of deleterious phases, with subsequent room-temperature tensile testing under standardized conditions.
generation.structural_mediator: The formation of a continuous or semi-continuous nanoscale ductile film along the internal boundaries within the lamellar colonies.
generation.mechanism: The interfacial films improve the bonding between lamellae by filling microstructural discontinuities, thereby inhibiting the initiation and propagation of microcracks. At the same time, they contribute to load transfer and delay localized deformation, leading to a simultaneous improvement in strength and ductility.
generation.predicted_outcome: Compared to the as-solidified baseline, the annealed specimens will display higher yield and ultimate tensile strengths and demonstrably larger tensile elongations during room-temperature deformation.
generation.baseline: The unmodified eutectic high-entropy alloy with brittle lamellar colonies where microcrack initiation at internal boundaries limits ductility.
generation.boundary: This intervention is expected to be effective under conditions where the annealing parameters reliably induce the targeted interfacial films without causing coarsening of the lamellar structure or the formation of other brittle phases. The effect may be limited if the alloy chemistry or processing window is outside the optimal range for controlled solute segregation.
generation.uncertainty: The quantitative extent to which the interfacial film formation can improve both strength and ductility is yet to be fully determined; optimal annealing parameters and their reproducibility across different alloy batches remain to be experimentally verified.

falsification_experiment.design: Prepare multiple batches of the eutectic high-entropy alloy and apply a series of controlled sub-annealing heat treatments spanning a range of temperatures and durations expected to induce solute segregation. Characterize the microstructure with electron microscopy (TEM/EBSD) to confirm the presence and continuity of nanoscale interfacial films. Conduct room-temperature tensile tests to compare mechanical properties against as-solidified samples.
measurements: TEM and EBSD imaging to detect and quantify the interfacial film characteristics at lamellar boundaries
Tensile strength, yield strength, and elongation at failure from standardized room-temperature tensile tests
falsification_experiment.falsification_rule: If specimens receiving the heat treatment do not display both (a) measurable formation of continuous nanoscale interfacial films at colony boundaries and (b) statistically significant improvements in both tensile strength and ductility compared to the as-solidified baseline, then the hypothesis is falsified.
